text: A suspended graphene monolayer absorbs a fixed roughly 2.3% of normally incident light, essentially independent of wavelength. This universal value equals:
choices: pi times the fine-structure constant (pi times alpha)
The square of the material's refractive index
The Landauer bound k_B T ln 2 in electron-volts
explanation: A graphene monolayer's approximately 2.3% absorption equals pi times the fine-structure constant alpha (about 1/137), a universal, wavelength-flat value flowing from the gapless Dirac spectrum and the universal sheet optical conductivity. It is not set by refractive index, numerical aperture, or the Landauer thermodynamic bound.
